Replay Global Error Controller

Replay Global Error is a controller that participates in pipeline arbitration when a global Vault error is present. It evaluates execution attempts and determines whether pipeline execution attempts are denied during a global error and whether previously blocked attempts may be retried once the error condition changes.

This controller operates within the Policy stage and does not observe or modify state values directly. Instead, it responds to pipeline attempt messages and global error signals to influence execution outcomes through controller voting.

When a global error is active, the controller denies pipeline attempts associated with the current execution trace. When the error condition is cleared, the controller may trigger a revote for previously denied attempts, allowing normal pipeline execution to resume.

Replay Global Error does not enqueue values, transform state, or inject side effects. Its responsibility is limited to coordinating retry and replay decisions in response to global error lifecycle events.

Note

When a global Vault error is active, pipeline execution remains paused until an external action explicitly clears the error state. Clearing the global error is performed by invoking VaultErrorServiceClass().clear(), which removes the active error signal and allows controllers and interceptors that depend on global error state to resume normal operation.

Until the global error is cleared, new pipeline attempts may be denied and previously blocked executions will not be replayed. This design ensures that recovery from global error conditions is explicit, intentional, and fully controlled by the application rather than occurring implicitly or automatically.

Additional Help

Global Error Handler
Design Decisions

The featureCellKey field on VaultErrorShape provides optional contextual information about which FeatureCell originated an error. This metadata allows applications to distinguish between globally blocking failures and FeatureCell-scoped errors when deciding how recovery should occur.

When an error represents a system-level failure—such as a backend outage, corrupted environment state, or violated consistency invariant—the featureCellKey may be ignored. In these cases, the error is treated as global, and all FeatureCells using Global Error Pause and Replay Global Error are paused uniformly until the error condition is explicitly cleared.

For user-facing or localized failures, the featureCellKey may be used by application logic to determine which FeatureCells should participate in recovery. This enables targeted remediation flows—such as retry prompts, authentication recovery, or domain-specific correction—without requiring a full application-wide pause.

The Replay Global Error controller does not interpret or filter errors based on featureCellKey. Instead, the field exists to support higher-level recovery decisions made by the application. Once VaultErrorServiceClass.clear() is invoked, the controller re-evaluates previously blocked execution attempts and allows normal pipeline arbitration to resume according to the updated global error state.

This design ensures that error scoping remains an application concern, while the pipeline maintains deterministic pause, replay, and recovery semantics regardless of how errors are classified or resolved.

Not all failures should be treated as global. Most domain-level errors — such as validation failures, rejected user input, business rule violations, or expected backend responses — should remain FeatureCell-scoped and handled locally within the pipeline using standard error behaviors. These errors do not require pausing other FeatureCells or halting application-wide execution.

The Replay Global Error controller is intended only for system-level or consistency-critical failures where continued state mutation could produce invalid or incoherent application state. Examples include backend outages, authentication invalidation, corrupted environment state, or invariant violations.

If an error affects only a single FeatureCell and does not threaten application-wide consistency, a local error handling strategy is preferred. Global error pause should be reserved for failures that require deliberate, coordinated recovery across multiple FeatureCells.

Diagram
Configuration

The Replay Global Error Controller is a structural policy controller that participates in pipeline execution arbitration when a global Vault error is present. Controllers do not observe or modify state values directly and are not configured through fluent APIs.

This controller is registered once during FeatureCell definition. Its configuration is declarative and static: no parameters are accepted, and behavior does not vary per invocation. Once registered, the controller remains active for the lifetime of the FeatureCell.

Because this controller participates in execution arbitration, it must be present before any pipeline execution begins. Registering it at definition time ensures that all pipeline attempts are consistently evaluated against global error conditions from the moment the FeatureCell is initialized.

During execution, the controller evaluates update attempts associated with a given pipeline trace and issues authoritative votes that determine whether an attempt is allowed to proceed, denied, or retried. When global error state changes, the controller may request revotes to ensure previously blocked or denied executions are reconsidered under the updated conditions.

This design enforces deterministic error recovery behavior and prevents runtime mutation of controller configuration. Global error handling rules are established once at definition time and remain stable throughout the FeatureCell lifecycle.

Registering the Replay Global Error Controller

The Replay Global Error Controller is attached structurally when the FeatureCell is defined. This determines that the FeatureCell participates in error-based execution control at runtime.

Registering the controller does configure the controller by itself.

{{`// app.config.ts

export const appConfig: ApplicationConfig = {
  providers: [
    provideVault({ logLevel: 'off' }),

    provideFeatureCell(
      EmployeeService
      {  
        key: 'employees',
        initialState: [],
      },
      [
        // Optional add-on behaviors
      ],
      [
        // Attach the Replay Global Error Controller structurally
        withReplayGlobalErrorController
      ]
    )
  ]
};
`}}
 
{{`export const employeeCell = FeatureCell<Employee[]>(
  {
    key: 'employees',
    initialState: [],
  },
  [
    // Optional add-on behaviors
  ],
  [
    // Attach the Replay Global Error Controller structurally
    withReplayGlobalErrorController
  ]
);`}}

);`}}
When to Use Replay Global Error

The Replay Global Error controller is intended for scenarios where pipeline execution must be explicitly paused during a global failure and resumed only after a deliberate recovery action. The table below outlines common situations where this controller is appropriate and the expected recovery strategy for each.

Scenario Recommended Usage Recovery Action
Critical backend failure

Global (all FeatureCells)

Ignore VaultErrorShape featureCellKey

Block all incoming state updates while the application is in an unrecoverable error state to prevent inconsistent or partial mutations. Log the error, resolve the underlying issue, then explicitly clear the global error using VaultErrorService.clear().
User-facing blocking error

Local (single FeatureCells)

Conditional on VaultErrorShape featureCellKey

Pause pipeline execution while prompting the user to take corrective action, such as retrying an operation or re-authenticating. Clear the global error after the user completes the recovery flow, allowing blocked attempts to be replayed.
Strict consistency requirements

Global (all FeatureCells)

Ignore VaultErrorShape featureCellKey

Ensure no state transitions occur while the application is in an invalid or indeterminate state caused by a global error. Perform validation or reconciliation, then clear the error to trigger controlled replay through the controller.
Examples

withReplayGlobalErrorController is a structural controller that must be attached when defining a FeatureCell. It is not registered through a fluent API and cannot be added dynamically after initialization.

In this example, the FeatureCell is defined with both the Global Error Pause interceptor and the Replay Global Error controller. While a global Vault error is active, incoming state updates are blocked at the Interceptor stage and execution attempts are denied through controller arbitration.

Pipeline execution remains paused until an external recovery action explicitly clears the global error using VaultErrorServiceClass.clear(). Once the error is cleared, previously blocked attempts are re-evaluated and replayed through the controller, allowing normal pipeline execution to resume in a deterministic and controlled manner.

Example 1: Configure a FeatureCell with Replay Global Error 

{{`// app.config.ts

export const appConfig: ApplicationConfig = {
  providers: [
    provideVault(),

    provideFeatureCell(
      EmployeeService,
      {
        key: 'employees',
        initialState: []
      },
      [
        // Additional add-on behaviors 
      ],
      [
        // REQUIRED: Coordinates replay and retry once the error is cleared
        withReplayGlobalErrorController
      ]
    )
  ]
};`}}

Example 2: Configure a Service

{{`
@FeatureCell<Employee[][]>('employees')
@Injectable({
  providedIn: 'root'
})
export class EmployeeService {
  private readonly vault = injectVault<Employee[][]>(EmployeeService);

  constructor() {
    this.vault.initialize();
  }
}`}}

Example 3: Observe and Clear a Global Vault Error

{{`import { VaultErrorService } from '@sdux-vault/shared';

// Obtain the singleton service
const errorService = VaultErrorService();

// Listen for global Vault error changes
const subscription = errorService.error$.subscribe((error) => {
  if (error) {
    console.info('Global Vault error detected:', error.message);
  } else {
    console.info('Global Vault error cleared');
  }
});

// At some later point (user action, recovery flow, retry button, etc.)
errorService.clear();

// Cleanup when no longer needed
subscription.unsubscribe();`}}
